title: Attn Switchboard tuner for prefill latency safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: On mixed workloads (variable seq-len, mixed prefill and decode bursts, and heterogeneous GPU pools) we observe 2x-4x variance in tail latency when the runtime switches attention implementations mid-request or during warmstarts. Current heuristics pick a single attention kernel per model invocation based on static seqlen bucketing; this is brittle for bursty prefill-heavy workloads and leads to P99 violations and increased cost from conservative fallbacks.

Goal: Build an "Attn Switchboard Tuner" that: (1) uses lightweight offline microbench fingerprints + a short online probing phase to choose attention kernels per-request, (2) applies distinct policies for prefill vs decode phases, (3) enforces latency safety via a rollback/backoff mechanism and ramp profiles to avoid flapping, and (4) exposes tunable knobs for Dedicated and Private customers (latency SLO, cost bias, exploration budget).

Design highlights and heuristics: 
- Offline fingerprinting: a background profiler records small microbenchmarks across available attention primitives (flash-attn variants, blockwise, memory-saver) for target seq-len buckets and model size classes. Results feed a per-arch lookup with median/90/99 latency and memory curves. Stored as compressed CSVs per-arch and model family.
- Warmstart policy: on cold start, use fingerprint lookup to pick a default kernel for prefill and a (potentially different) default for decode. Prefill selection prefers memory-stable kernels when KV cache allocations are large; decode selection biases lower-latency kernels for short-token steps.
- Online small-probe phase: for first N requests (configurable, default 4) do a controlled epsilon-greedy probe across 2-3 top candidates within the same performance band. Probes are micro-batched where possible to reduce cost. Probe outcomes update a lightweight epochal estimator (EWMA of latency and memory pressure).
- Safety envelope and rollback: maintain per-request and per-route latency budgets. If probe or production kernel yields P95 > SLO or OOM risk > threshold, automatically fall back to conservative kernel and reduce exploration rate. Rollback includes an exponential backoff and a slow ramp to re-enable exploration.
- Phase-aware scheduling: treat prefill and decode separately — prefill picks for total memory consumption and sustained throughput; decode picks for per-token latency and cache locality. When switching mid-request (e.g., prefill->decode), we allow different kernel choices without warm restart of runtime but with KV cache compatibility checks.
- Heterogeneous pools: preference table contains per-GPU fingerprints and a short compatibility check. If target kernel not available on chosen GPU, runtime will either: (a) remap request to compatible GPU (if routing policy allows), or (b) use nearest neighbor kernel with cost penalty estimate.

Trade-offs and rationale: 
- Exploration vs SLO risk: we cap exploration aggressively for routes with strict SLOs. For best-effort routes we allow higher exploration budgets to reduce unit cost over time.
- Memory vs latency: many memory-saver kernels reduce peak memory at cost of throughput; prefill-heavy workloads benefit from memory-stable kernels to avoid node-level OOMs.
- Operational complexity: we keep the online learner lightweight (EWMA + small probe count) to avoid long-lived bandit state and make behavior debuggable in logs and console.

Data and metrics to track: 
- Per-route: probe success rate, exploration budget remaining, chosen kernel per phase, P50/P95/P99 latency, memory headroom, fallback frequency, cost/change in tokens/sec.
- Cluster-level: distribution of kernel choices per-arch, rollback events per hour, routing remap rate, customer-facing error rate.

Rollout plan: 
1) Prototype in runtime branch: runtime/attn-switchboard-proto (see PR below). Instrument microbench harness and expose probe toggles.
2) Canary on infra test cluster with synthetic prefill-heavy traces (50k requests/day) — track rollback events and tail latency.
3) Gradual ramp to low-SLO tenants with exploration=0.05, then widen.
4) GA with console knobs + recommended defaults for Dedicated and Private.

Artifacts and links: 
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Attn+Switchboard+Tuner
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4873
- Microbench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/tools/attn_microbench (branch attn-switchboard-proto)
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/attn-switchboard-canary (temporary)

Open questions and risks: 
- How to represent multi-kernel compatibility when quantized kernels differ (INT8 vs FP16)? Proposed: include quantization dimension in fingerprint key and disallow probing across quantization domains unless safe casting path exists.
- Long-term state storage: current plan uses ephemeral EWMA in runtime and persists offline fingerprints. We need an optional persisted bandit state for Dedicated customers who want stable per-tenant tuning.
- Hot-path instrumentation overhead: ensure probe latency + metrics emit doesn't add >2% overhead to P50.

Next steps: 
- Finish microbench harness integration and run a 24h sweep across our heterogeneous GPU pool (task assigned below).
- Add console controls for exploration budget and SLO override.
- Coordinate with routing team to allow remap policies for kernel availability.
